headline: Aerobic base and easy-run efficiency remain firmly intact, but the block still lacks any loaded or back-to-back durability work.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic engine is in a good place. Easy-run HR continues to sit meaningfully lower on comparable efforts than the prior period, and volume has held essentially flat across the two blocks — this is a consolidation window, not regression. Nothing in the data suggests any loss of fitness; if anything, the efficiency signal has been consistent enough now over several weeks that it reads as a genuine adaptation rather than noise.

The gap worth naming again is durability-specific work. With the crossing about a month out and a self-supported, multi-day, pack-loaded profile, the current block is still built around single-session road runs at moderate distance. Your longest recent effort and your day-to-day terrain don't yet reflect the sustained time-on-feet or consecutive-day demand the route will impose. This isn't an urgent alarm — your base and demonstrated ultra history give you real headroom — but it's the one dimension the recent data hasn't touched.

Strength frequency has stepped up noticeably and is sitting well above the prior block, which is a positive for pack-carrying resilience. The question is whether that raised frequency stays compatible if running-specific durability volume does start entering the picture.
watch_items: Whether any pack-loaded or consecutive-day efforts finally enter the block as the crossing approaches.
Whether per-session elevation and duration begin trending upward to reflect sustained hilly terrain.
Whether the elevated strength frequency and any added running durability work can coexist without compromising either.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 143 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 7 runs)
▼ 4-week volume 128 km vs 133 km prior block (-4%)
